source_quote: 8th day of the second tenday of Myrkhul 1495

subject: 8th day of the second tenday of Myrkhul 1495

source_quote: Today, we arrive at Neverlight Grove.

subject: Day of Joy
fact: The 'Day of Joy' is a ritual date proclaimed by Phylo, likely tied to the activation of the Circle of Masters' final ritual, possibly coinciding with the arrival of the next group of 'softers' or the full manifestation of Zuggtomy’s influence.
source_quote: Celebrate as the day of joy is nigh!

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during a single session of play, marked by the progression of combat, dialogue, and tactical planning from the retrieval of the Grick to the discovery of the Shambling Mound.
source_quote: And soon enough, we arrive at one of the mounds.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the second tenday of Myrkhul 1495 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: tomorrow
fact: The 'great celebration' promised by Phylo is scheduled for tomorrow, tying the entire narrative arc to an imminent, potentially catastrophic event. The party’s current actions — the quest completion, the architectural discussions, the unresolved mysteries — all converge on this single temporal anchor.
source_quote: I wonder if this has anything to do with the celebration promised by Phylo tomorrow.

subject: Activation of Dawnbringer's Light
fact: When Thorin picked up the hilt, Dawnbringer manifested a shimmering blade of light where none existed, confirming its sentient nature and magical power. This event marked the sword’s full awakening and integration into the party’s arsenal.
source_quote: Thorin... picks up the magical hilt. The sword rejoices, and then, where there is no blade, a shimmering blade of light appears.

subject: arrival at Neverlight Grove
fact: The party arrives at Neverlight Grove after traversing the Underdark, and is awed by its bioluminescent beauty, only to discover its hidden dangers and political fractures.
source_quote: Today, we arrive at Neverlight Grove. ... As we enter the cave, the beauty overwhelms Grygum, who shouts, “Wow, this place is incredible.” ... Basidia warns us the grove is not safe.

subject: arrival at Neverlight Grove
fact: The party enters Neverlight Grove after days of travel through the Underdark. The cavern is a bioluminescent wonder filled with glowing fungi, myconids, and strange constellations on the ceiling. It is a sanctuary of beauty and life, starkly contrasting the darkness they have endured.
source_quote: ‘Wow, this place is incredible.’

source_quote: Phylo insists that all dead creatures must be brought to the Circle of Masters. ... To reanimate.

subject: reanimation of the Grick
fact: The Grick’s corpse was retrieved from the battlefield and is intended for reanimation by Basidia, per Phylo’s doctrine. Reanimation transforms the dead into tactical assets, not food.
source_quote: If you could bring this creature to Basidia, she could reanimate it, and it could help you.

subject: recognition of Sarith’s infected spores
fact: Basidia identifies Sarith’s spores as unnatural and different from those of other myconid sovereigns, indicating Zuggtomy’s influence.
source_quote: I do not recognize the spores of this drow. ... Poor Sarith has been affected by Zuggtomy.

subject: request to hunt the grick
fact: Loobamub asks the party to retrieve a grick for reanimation by Basidia, revealing the myconids’ role as collectors, not killers.
source_quote: Loobamub listens to Basidia, and then he turns to me and asks if we could help him deal with a grick. ... We bring back the dead. We do not kill.

subject: revelation of the ‘two in a box’
fact: The co-sovereignty of Phylo and Basidia mirrors the Menzoberranzan practice of ‘two in a box’ — a forced power-sharing arrangement that signifies political weakness and often leads to mutual destruction. Daz recognizes this as a dangerous precedent, foreshadowing collapse.
source_quote: ‘We used the term, ‘two in a box’ to describe this power sharing… The box was a metaphor for a tomb.’

subject: Rump-a-dump
fact: Rump-a-dump shouted, “We’re home!” upon entering the cavern.
source_quote: And then I hear Rump-a-dump's delight and Stool’s happiness as they run into the cavern shouting, “We’re home!”

subject: Sarith's infection
fact: Sarith the drow guide has been infected by Zuggtomy’s demonic spores, recognizable to Basidia.
source_quote: I do not recognize the spores of this drow... Poor Sarith has been affected by Zuggtomy

subject: Shambling Mound encounter
fact: A Shambling Mound is concealed in the swampy ground near the Circle of Hunters’ territory, camouflaged as moss.
source_quote: a Shambling Mound is concealed nearby, lurking like mossy camouflage within the swampy ground

subject: Spore Recognition Failure
fact: Basidia’s inability to recognize the spores of the drow (or infected myconid) indicates a fundamental breach in myconid sensory biology, confirming that the corruption is not natural but foreign and demonic in origin.
source_quote: Every myconid sovereign can recognize the spores of any other sovereign in the Underdark. This is strange.

subject: Stool
fact: Stool shouted, “We’re home!” upon entering the cavern.
source_quote: And then I hear Rump-a-dump's delight and Stool’s happiness as they run into the cavern shouting, “We’re home!”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin and his sword raced down into the cavern with the rest.
source_quote: Thorin and his sword race down with the rest.

subject: travel to Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is approximately eight days away via the Underdark.
source_quote: we arrive at Neverlight Grove

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Two in a Box
fact: The term 'two in a box' refers to a failed power-sharing arrangement in Menzoberranzan, where two co-rulers are appointed due to indecision, often leading to their mutual destruction.
source_quote: We used the term, 'two in a box' to describe this power sharing... The box from our saying was a metaphor for a tomb

subject: use of K’tharr-li to detect the shambling mound
fact: Daz applies the childhood game K’tharr-li to detect the hidden shambling mound by freezing terrain in five-foot cubes to reveal anomalies.
source_quote: I visualize the terrain as a precise grid, and intend to freeze five-foot cube sections of the moss and water using Shape Water. ... When I was a child, there was a game we played called K’tharr-li.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir asked Basidia for a spore to identify themselves as allies.
source_quote: Can you give us some kind of spore, so other myconids will know we work for you?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir asked if the spore infecting Phylo is the same as the one infecting Sarith.
source_quote: Is it the same spore that infects Sarith?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted the creature was felled by persistent magic, not a final weapon strike.
source_quote: The creature is felled not by a final weapon strike, but by the relentless, quiet efficacy of persistent magic.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observed the creature attempting to consume Thorin while still grappled.
source_quote: The image is strange—I hold it, yet it tries to consume another.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir opened the invisible chest after Daz outlined it.
source_quote: Using fairy fire, I outline the box, and Zalthir opens it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized he had a reason to grapple.
source_quote: I think, "I have a reason to grapple."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir refused to be drowned by the creature's grappling ability.
source_quote: I decide that I do not wish to be drowned

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said to Grygum, “What, you don't want a zombie grick joining our team? That sounds so fun.”
source_quote: I turn to him and say - “What, you don't want a zombie grick joining our team? That sounds so fun.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought of the reanimated creatures from the Whorlstone Caves and shuddered.
source_quote: I think to myself of the reanimated creatures I saw in the Whorlstone Caves and shudder.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir used his monastic deflection technique to absorb bludgeoning force.
source_quote: I use my monastic deflection technique, absorbing a portion of the bludgeoning force and limiting the pain.

subject: Zuggtomy reference
fact: Zuggtomy is a deity often referred to with feminine pronouns, unusual among myconids, raising suspicion of corruption.
source_quote: I remember that Zuggtomy is often referred to as she. And I worry.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is an organization of Myconid Sovereigns who maintain ritual control over the Neverlight Grove, oversee the animation of slain creatures for the Basidia, and enforce cultural protocols tied to Phylo’s impending 'great awakening'. They treat surface-world concepts with detached authority and prioritize the continuity of their own traditions.
source_quote: The animation will continue and be successful.

subject: Circle of Hunters
fact: The Circle of Hunters gathers the remains of slain creatures and delivers them to the Circle of Masters for reanimation. They follow Phylo’s new doctrine of non-killing and operate under Basidia’s indirect influence, though their loyalty is now divided.
source_quote: ‘We bring back the dead. We do not kill.’

subject: Circle of Hunters
fact: The Circle of Hunters is a functional myconid faction within Neverlight Grove that brings in carcasses, which are now being intercepted and exploited by the Circle of Masters, suggesting a power shift and hidden agenda.
source_quote: the Circle of Masters is taking most of the carcasses the Circle of Hunters bring in...

subject: Circle of Hunters
fact: The Circle of Hunters is a myconid sub-group under Phylo’s doctrine, tasked with retrieving corpses from the wild for reanimation by the Circle of Masters. They do not kill, only recover the dead.
source_quote: Loobamub, the leader of the Circle of Hunters, tells us as we leave that a Shambling Mound is concealed nearby...

subject: Circle of Masters
fact: The Circle of Masters is a myconid hierarchy within Phylo’s doctrine, composed of the most trusted leaders who oversee the reanimation of all dead creatures brought to them. They are the central authority for resurrection and tactical reassignment of the undead.
source_quote: And then there is the Inner Circle and the Circle of Masters… The Inner Circle of all of the circle leaders and the Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo.

subject: Circle of Masters
fact: The Circle of Masters is a rogue faction within Neverlight Grove that has taken control of the Garden of Welcome, is harvesting carcasses from the Circle of Hunters, sending myconids outside the grove in secret, and is likely responsible for the demonic spore infection affecting Phylo and others.
source_quote: the Circle of Masters is taking most of the carcasses the Circle of Hunters bring in, and are sending groups of myconids outside the grove without telling anybody.

subject: Circle of Masters
fact: The Circle of Masters is a secretive myconid faction aligned with Phylo, responsible for reanimating dead creatures and conducting rituals in the Garden of Welcome. They are suspected of harvesting corpses from outside the grove and are the epicenter of the corruption spreading through Neverlight Grove.
source_quote: ‘The Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome.’

subject: Circle of the Builders
fact: The Circle of the Builders is a Drow organization within the Neverlight Grove, associated with architectural and structural experimentation under the influence of Sovereign Phylo, where Myconids like Gasbide pursue radical construction concepts.
source_quote: Basidia then leads us toward the next segment of this bizarre cultural tour: the Circle of the Builders.

subject: Circle of the Masters
fact: The Circle of the Masters is a myconid faction that reanimates corpses, removes members from the grove, and is suspected of being corrupted by demonic spores.
source_quote: The Circle of Masters is taking most of the carcasses the Circle of Hunters bring in, and are sending groups of myconids outside the grove without telling anybody.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow are a subterranean elven race who pursued the party through the Underdark. They are now believed to have been lost on the trail. Sarith, their guide, is a lone representative who exhibits ambivalence toward the Myconids and their home.
source_quote: Eldeth told us this morning that she believed we had lost them. They were no longer on our trail.

subject: Inner Circle
fact: The Inner Circle consists of the leaders of all other myconid circles and the sovereigns. Phylo has restricted their interactions to only other circle leaders, breaking the traditional unity of the myconid society and isolating them from the broader community.
source_quote: ‘Phylo decided that each circle would meld exclusively with its circle, and only the circle leaders would meld with other circle leaders and the sovereigns.’

subject: Inner Circle
fact: The Inner Circle is the elite tier of Phylo’s hierarchy, composed of the closest advisors and circle leaders who enforce his doctrine and maintain the reanimation pipeline. They are the core of ideological control.
source_quote: And then there is the Inner Circle and the Circle of Masters… The Inner Circle of all of the circle leaders and the Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo.

subject: Myconids
fact: The Myconids are a sentient fungal race that live in harmony with Neverlight Grove. They glow with bioluminescent light, communicate joy through vocalizations, and consider the grove their home. Some are affected by a mysterious disease, but they remain integral to the ecosystem.
source_quote: Myconids, the mushroom folk we're traveling with, are everywhere, and they seem to be a part of this vibrant world... the mysterious disease affecting the Myconids.

subject: Myconids
fact: The myconids are sentient fungal beings who live in Neverlight Grove, organized into circles, and are now divided by Phylo’s new social order.
source_quote: Myconids, the mushroom folk we're traveling with, are everywhere, and they seem to be a part of this vibrant world... Each circle gathers around a circle mound... Phylo decided that each circle would meld exclusively with its circle...

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a myconid community under spiritual and biological siege, where social order has been disrupted by the Circle of Masters, the sovereign Phylo is corrupted, and the true ruler Basidia is powerless to act without risking infection.
source_quote: Phylo has changed the social order of the community. There are many circles in the Neverlight Grove, and each circle serves a function.

subject: Phylo
fact: Phylo is a chaotic Myconid Sovereign whose influence drives the 'great awakening' and 'great celebration' promised to the Myconids. His teachings inspire dangerous architectural fantasies, such as building towers to breach the Underdark, and foster ignorance of surface-world dangers like sunlight. He is the central figure of a cultic movement within the Neverlight Grove.
source_quote: It is part of a great celebration to come.

subject: The Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a group of companions who follow Daz’s plan to use Shape Water to detect the shambling mound.
source_quote: I tell The Ember Vanguard that I have a plan to neutralize the creature’s ability to hide.

subject: access tunnel to Neverlight Grove
fact: The access tunnel to Neverlight Grove is a natural formation created by a drying underground stream, dimly lit by lichen, and opens above the grove’s main floor.
source_quote: We have just entered this magical place from a natural tunnel that was formed by a drying underground stream, and that is dimly lit by lichen. The access tunnel opens above the grove’s main floor.

subject: central basin of Neverlight Grove
fact: The central basin of Neverlight Grove contains a clear pool, a dry central mound, and is surrounded by a fungal forest covering every surface including the ceiling.
source_quote: Beyond the mud and mushrooms of the fungal forest, a large, clear pool sits in the midst of the fungal grove. A central mound is the only dry spot in sight...

subject: Circle Mound
fact: A Circle Mound is a pile of rocks and soil upon which mold, lichen, and mushrooms grow, around which each myconid circle gathers to sleep.
source_quote: each circle gathers around a circle mound, which they describe as a pile of rocks and soil upon which mold, lichen, and mushrooms grow

subject: Circle of Hunters
fact: The Circle of Hunters is a myconid circle responsible for bringing back dead creatures to the Circle of Masters for reanimation.
source_quote: Loobamub. ... Phylo insists that all dead creatures must be brought to the Circle of Masters. ... We bring back the dead. We do not kill.

subject: Circle of Masters
fact: The Circle of Masters is a group of myconids closest to Phylo who reanimate dead creatures and send myconids outside the grove without explanation.
source_quote: The Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo. ... The Circle of Masters is taking most of the carcasses the Circle of Hunters bring in, and are sending groups of myconids outside the grove without telling anybody.

subject: Eastern Plateau
fact: The Eastern Plateau is a forbidden zone in Neverlight Grove, where the Circle of Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise, likely the activation point of a larger demonic ritual or portal tied to Zuggtomy’s influence.
source_quote: But please, don’t visit the eastern plateau because the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome.

subject: Eastern Plateau
fact: The Eastern Plateau is a restricted area where the Circle of the Masters is preparing a mysterious event.
source_quote: please, don’t visit the eastern plateau because the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise

subject: eastern plateau
fact: The eastern plateau is a forbidden zone where the Circle of Masters prepares a mysterious and glorious surprise, and where visitors vanish.
source_quote: Please, don’t visit the eastern plateau because the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome.

subject: Eastern Plateau
fact: The eastern plateau is the location of the Garden of Welcome, a forbidden zone where corrupted myconids conduct mysterious rites. It is shrouded in mist and lies beyond the central basin, accessible only through hidden paths.
source_quote: ‘I can give you a peek tomorrow, if you want.’

subject: False Tomb of Brysis
fact: The False Tomb of Brysis is a decoy sarcophagus designed to appear as a resting place for a powerful undead entity. It is easily opened and contains treasure, but was magically linked to a trap that dissipated upon Brysis’s death. It was warned against by Fargas Rumblefoot.
source_quote: This was the false tomb, complete with a sarcophagus that was very easy to open. This was the place that Fargas Rumblefoot warned us of.

subject: Garden of Welcome
fact: The Garden of Welcome is a central location within Neverlight Grove where visitors are taken by Phylo, but it is now a site of capture and corruption, used by the Circle of Masters to process infected myconids and 'softers' into the demonic spore network.
source_quote: They were taken to the Garden of Welcome. I haven’t seen them since...

subject: Garden of Welcome
fact: The Garden of Welcome is a forbidden area of Neverlight Grove where the Circle of Masters performs rituals. It is the site of disappearances and reanimation. Basidia warns against entering, but suspects it holds the key to understanding Phylo’s corruption.
source_quote: ‘Please, don’t visit the eastern plateau because the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise…’

subject: Garden of Welcome
fact: The Garden of Welcome is a forbidden area where the Circle of the Masters prepares a wondrous and glorious surprise, and where previous 'softers' have disappeared.
source_quote: Please, don’t visit the eastern plateau because the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome. ... Another group of 'softers' arrived not too many cycles ago and accepted Phylo’s offer. They were taken to the Garden of Welcome. I haven’t seen them since, nor has Phylo made any further mention of them.

subject: Garden of Welcome
fact: The Garden of Welcome is a forbidden area where the Circle of the Masters prepares a wondrous surprise and takes in myconids and carcasses without explanation.
source_quote: the Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome

subject: Garden of Welcome
fact: The Garden of Welcome is a sacred yet dangerous site where the Circle of Masters performs unknown rites, and where those who enter do not return.
source_quote: The Circle of the Masters is preparing a wondrous and glorious surprise in the Garden of Welcome. ... I haven’t seen them since, nor has Phylo made any further mention of them.

subject: great circle of the Masters
fact: The great circle of the Masters is the central gathering place of the Circle of Masters, where they perform rites and prepare their wondrous and glorious surprise.
source_quote: Phylo said that everything would be more efficient and better. Many of the myconids have followed Phylo and his new ways. ... I shall take them to the great circle of the Masters.

subject: Inner Circle
fact: The Inner Circle consists of all circle leaders and is separate from the Circle of Masters, though both are part of Phylo’s new social order.
source_quote: Phylo decided that each circle would meld exclusively with its circle, and only the circle leaders would meld with other circle leaders and the sovereigns. ... The Inner Circle of all of the circle leaders and the Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo.

subject: Inner Circle
fact: The Inner Circle consists of all circle leaders and is separate from the Circle of Masters, which is composed of those closest to Phylo.
source_quote: The Inner Circle of all of the circle leaders and the Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo.

subject: Lake near the shore
fact: The lake is more than 10 feet deep and serves as the battleground where Zalthir uses his Stunning Strike and grapple to trap the Shambling Mound. It is circled by the party to avoid drowning, emphasizing tactical awareness of terrain and creature capabilities.
source_quote: The creature is near the shore of a lake that is more than 10 feet deep.

subject: lake shore
fact: The lake shore is a 10-foot-deep body of water where Zalthir engaged the Grick from a safe distance, avoiding grappling threats. It is a tactical chokepoint in the swamp.
source_quote: The creature is near the shore of a lake that is more than 10 feet deep.

subject: mossy swamp
fact: The mossy swamp is a treacherous, waterlogged terrain concealing hidden undead entities like the Shambling Mound and the Grick. It is the primary hunting ground for the Circle of Hunters and the site of recent combat.
source_quote: Loobamub... tells us that a Shambling Mound is concealed nearby, lurking like mossy camouflage within the swampy ground.

subject: mound of the Circle of Hunters
fact: The mound of the Circle of Hunters is a pile of rocks and soil where Loobamub and his circle gather to sleep and prepare dead creatures for the Circle of Masters.
source_quote: Each circle gathers around a circle mound, which they describe as a pile of rocks and soil upon which mold, lichen, and mushrooms grow. ... Loobamub. ... We bring back the dead.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a fungal ecosystem centered around fungal mounds where myconids sleep, now corrupted by demonic spores, hidden transmissions, and a fractured leadership structure between Phylo and Basidia.
source_quote: Each circle gathers around a circle mound, which they describe as a pile of rocks and soil upon which mold, lichen, and mushrooms grow.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a vast cavern with bioluminescent walls, glowing myconids, and a central basin containing a clear pool and a giant mushroom visible in the distance.
source_quote: As we enter the cave, the beauty overwhelms Grygum, who shouts, “Wow, this place is incredible.” ... The cave walls shimmer with a soft, bioluminescent light, casting a gentle glow on everything. The light is a beautiful mosaic of blues, greens, and purples, like a nebula trapped underground. ... A central mound is the only dry spot in sight, though a small cliff rises above the cavern floor far across the clearing with giant mushrooms visible in the distance.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a vast cavern with bioluminescent walls, glowing myconids, and a central basin containing a clear pool and a towering fungal forest covering ceiling and walls.
source_quote: the cave walls shimmer with a soft, bioluminescent light... Myconids... glowing with the same otherworldly light

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a vast, bioluminescent cavern in the Underdark, illuminated by living fungi that emit a mosaic of blues, greens, and purples. It is a cathedral-like environment teeming with Myconids, with a ceiling and walls covered in glowing fungal forests. It opens via a dimly lit tunnel formed by a dried underground stream, and beyond lies a narrow ravine leading to a distant majestic mushroom.
source_quote: We have just entered this magical place from a natural tunnel that was formed by a drying underground stream... the mushroom forest that covers every surface, including the ceiling...

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove is a vast, luminous cavern beneath the Underdark, illuminated by bioluminescent fungi that cover walls, ceiling, and ground. It contains a central pool, fungal forests, ravines, and hidden plateaus. It is the heart of myconid civilization, now under threat from corruption.
source_quote: ‘It's a living, breathing landscape of impossible color… a cathedral of light and life.’

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a subterranean Drow sanctuary where Myconids dwell under the influence of Sovereign Phylo, characterized by unnatural vegetation, faerzress, and the lingering presence of slain creatures such as the Grick.
source_quote: We return to the Neverlight Grove, the corpse of the Grick dragging slightly.

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: The Neverlight Grove is a subterranean ecosystem saturated with faerzress, glowing fungi, and channeled irrigation systems. It hosts the Circle of the Builders and Northern Terraces, where Myconids like Gasbide obsess over surface-world architecture. It is a site of ritual, cultural exchange, and hidden danger tied to Phylo’s influence.
source_quote: The terraces lining the northern walls are suffused with faerzress.

subject: Neverlight Grove Access Tunnel
fact: The access tunnel to Neverlight Grove is a natural formation carved by a drying underground stream, dimly lit by lichen.
source_quote: We have just entered this magical place from a natural tunnel that was formed by a drying underground stream, and that is dimly lit by lichen.

subject: Northern Terraces of the Neverlight Grove
fact: The Northern Terraces are a region of the Neverlight Grove filled with glowing fungi, trickling water channeled into irrigation systems, and a thick, sweet fungal aroma. It is where Gasbide approaches the party and begins his architectural interrogation, revealing the Grove’s deeper connection to Phylo’s dreams of surface breach.
source_quote: A thick, sweet smell fills the air from the thousands of fungi of all colors and sizes.

subject: Northern Terraces of the Neverlight Grove
fact: The Northern Terraces are a vast cavernous area lined with faerzress-infused walls, channeled irrigation systems, and dense glowing fungal vegetation, emitting a thick, sweet aroma from thousands of bioluminescent fungi.
source_quote: The terraces lining the northern walls are suffused with faerzress, and I notice that this place is filled with vegetation. As I draw closer, I see water trickling from the walls of this vast cavern being channeled into a crude yet effective terraced irrigation system.

subject: ravine beyond Neverlight Grove
fact: The ravine beyond Neverlight Grove narrows the cavern and is shrouded in mist, with smaller caverns visible beyond.
source_quote: Beyond the exotic forest, the cavern narrows into a ravine. And beyond the ravine, I catch a glimpse of a majestic mushroom... the darkness of the ravine and mist-shrouded smaller cavern beyond.

subject: Real Tomb of Brysis
fact: The Real Tomb of Brysis is the true resting place of the undead wraith, where Dawnbringer was found and the wraith was slain. It is connected to the False Tomb via passageways and contains the mummified corpse with the sword hilt held by withered hands.
source_quote: As we look around for treasure, we stumble on an invisible chest... Once we have collected the treasure of Brysis, we climb out of the real tomb...

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Whorlstone Caves
fact: The Whorlstone Caves are a known site of prior myconid reanimation activity, where reanimated creatures have been observed, contributing to the party’s unease about Phylo’s doctrine.
source_quote: I think to myself of the reanimated creatures I saw in the Whorlstone Caves and shudder.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is a myconid sovereign who opposes Phylo’s reforms and fears he has been infected by a diseased spore.
source_quote: I fear Phylo has contracted some kind of diseased spore... I believe this is contrary to the unity and harmony of our way of life

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Grick
fact: A grick is a predatory beast encountered in the swamp, known for its resistances and ambush tactics. It was slain by the Ember Vanguard after being stunned, blinded, and struck with fire and acid. Its corpse was retrieved for reanimation.
source_quote: The Grik hisses... The blinded Grick misses all three of its subsequent attacks... Thorin delivers the killing blow...

subject: Grick
fact: A grick is a predatory creature whose corpse Loobamub seeks to retrieve for reanimation. It is not killed by the myconids but found dead or captured, then delivered to the Circle of Masters for transformation into a reanimated servant.
source_quote: ‘Could you help him deal with a grick?’

subject: Grick
fact: The Grick is a creature resistant to fire, stunned by Zalthir’s Stunning Strike, and targeted by Daz’s Fireball. It is blinded by magical darkness, misses three attacks against the Ember Vanguard, flees predictably, and is killed by Thorin. Its corpse is retrieved for Basidia.
source_quote: The blinded Grick misses all three of its subsequent attacks against the Ember Vanguard.

subject: Grick
fact: The Grick is a slain creature whose corpse was dragged to Basidia and stripped of its head, indicating its use in ritual or material acquisition by the Drow.
source_quote: We return to the Neverlight Grove, the corpse of the Grick dragging slightly.

subject: Loobamub
fact: Loobamub is a myconid leader of the Circle of Hunters who brings dead creatures to the Circle of Masters for reanimation.
source_quote: Loobamub. ... We bring back the dead. We do not kill.

subject: Phylo
fact: Phylo is a myconid sovereign who has adopted a new social order, isolating circles and aligning with the Circle of Masters.
source_quote: Phylo decided that each circle would meld exclusively with its circle... The Circle of Masters is a circle of those who are closest to Phylo

subject: Shambling Mound
fact: A concealed shambling mound lurks near the fungal forest, camouflaged in moss and swamp. It is a deadly threat that grapples and crushes prey. Daz plans to neutralize it using Shape Water to detect its hidden form by identifying unfrozen sections of terrain.
source_quote: ‘A Shambling Mound is concealed nearby, lurking like mossy camouflage within the swampy ground.’

subject: Shambling Mound
fact: A shambling mound is a concealed, moss-covered undead entity lurking in the swampy ground, capable of grappling and ambush. It was located by Daz using a grid-based spell technique derived from K’tharr-li.
source_quote: Loobamub, the leader of the Circle of Hunters, tells us as we leave that a Shambling Mound is concealed nearby, lurking like mossy camouflage within the swampy ground.

subject: Shambling Mound
fact: The Shambling Mound is a swamp creature capable of grappling, engulfing, and attacking with tendrils. It is stunned by Zalthir, trapped within Grygum’s Spirit Guardians, and ultimately felled not by a single weapon strike but by the relentless cumulative damage of persistent magic. It attempts to escape and engulf Thorin but fails.
source_quote: It thrashes, using its tendril in an attempt to attack me, and succeeds.

subject: Zombie Grick
fact: The Grick is intended to be reanimated into a zombie, serving as a tactical asset for the party under Basidia’s authority. Its potential as a companion is mocked by Grygum as 'so fun,' but its true nature is horrifying.
source_quote: What, you don't want a zombie grick joining our team? That sounds so fun.

subject: Zuggtomy
fact: Zuggtomy is a demonic entity associated with fungal corruption and mind-altering spores, referenced as a goddess by infected characters, and likely the source of the demonic spore infecting Sarith, Zalthir, and Phylo.
source_quote: I remember that Zuggtomy is often referred to as she. And I worry.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is a myconid sovereign who leads followers in reanimating the dead, enforcing Phylo’s doctrine that efficiency comes from circle-based hierarchy and sovereign control. She has accepted Loobamub as a loyal follower and seeks corpses for reanimation.
source_quote: Basidia tells us that this is one of her followers, 'Loobamub.'

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is a myconid sovereign who opposes Phylo’s new social order and secretly warns outsiders of the dangers in the Garden of Welcome and the Circle of Masters.
source_quote: The other sovereign introduces itself as Basidia and says to Phylo, “I can take them on the tour of the gardens, co-sovereign.” ... I do not recognize the spores of this drow. ... I believe this is contrary to the unity and harmony of our way of life.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is a myconid sovereign who suspects Phylo is infected by a demonic spore, fears for the survival of the grove, has secretly provided the party with a scroll of protection against fiends and potions, and reveals that the Circle of Masters is harvesting carcasses and sending myconids outside the grove without authorization.
source_quote: The grove is not safe. Another group of 'softers' arrived not too many cycles ago and accepted Phylo’s offer. They were taken to the Garden of Welcome. I haven’t seen them since, nor has Phylo made any further mention of them.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is the Sovereign who accepts the Grick corpse and leads the group toward the Circle of the Builders, expressing concern for the continuation of the animation but affirming the presence and contentment of Rump-a-dump and Stool among their kind.
source_quote: We had stripped the Grik for its head. Basidia is concerned, but then sighs. The animation will continue and be successful.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is the Sovereign who accepts the Grick corpse and oversees the ritual animation of its remains. She leads the party through the Neverlight Grove’s cultural segments, dismisses Grygum’s requests to bring Rump-a-dump and Stool along, and confirms the completion of the quest after retrieving the corpse for the Basidia.
source_quote: We have completed the quest.

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia is the co-sovereign of Neverlight Grove, sharing power uneasily with Phylo. She is deeply concerned that Phylo has been infected by a corrupting spore and fears the consequences of his new social order. She secretly aids the party with potions, scrolls, and information, and can detect foreign spores.
source_quote: ‘I fear Phylo has contracted some kind of diseased spore… I will give you more treasures if you bring back my sovereign.’

subject: Basidia
fact: Basidia then leads us toward the next segment of this bizarre cultural tour: the Circle of the Builders.
source_quote: Basidia then leads us toward the next segment of this bizarre cultural tour: the Circle of the Builders.

subject: Basidia
fact: The Sovereign, Basidia, accepts the Grick. We had stripped the Grik for its head. Basidia is concerned, but then sighs. The animation will continue and be successful.
source_quote: The Sovereign, Basidia, accepts the Grick. We had stripped the Grik for its head. Basidia is concerned, but then sighs. The animation will continue and be successful.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a powerful sunblade that can read and write, and can cast lesser restoration. It speaks with a sentient voice, reacts to emotional cues, and manifests a shimmering blade of light where no physical blade exists. It insists on being helped and resists being left behind or extinguished.
source_quote: The sword introduces itself as Dawnbringer. A powerful sunblade that can read and write, and can cast lesser restoration.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade capable of reading, writing, and casting lesser restoration. It emits constant light and speaks with a willful, pleading tone. It claims to be the Dawnbringer and reacts emotionally to being ignored or rejected.
source_quote: ‘I can help you! Please don’t let me go.’ ‘Not Dawnbringer!’

subject: Daz
fact: "I'll nerd out with them for a little while," I tell everyone.
source_quote: "I'll nerd out with them for a little while," I tell everyone.

subject: Daz
fact: "Sure," I respond.
source_quote: "Sure," I respond.

subject: Daz
fact: And then we get into more technical discussions. Finally, a creature that can discuss the final points of construction and design with me.
source_quote: And then we get into more technical discussions. Finally, a creature that can discuss the final points of construction and design with me.

subject: Daz
fact: As I prepare to spew the caustic solution in the general direction of the creature, I note to Zalthir, "One of the material components is a toothbrush, you know, for afterward." You must keep your humor, even when covered in your own corrosive vomit.

subject: Daz
fact: Bahamut’s blessed creatures, the Brass Dragon, breathe acid. And the black dragon, which he teaches us is also a holy creature, breathes acid. So am I not, in a curious way, honoring my god in this way?
source_quote: Bahamut’s blessed creatures, the Brass Dragon, breathe acid. And the black dragon, which he teaches us is also a holy creature, breathes acid. So am I not, in a curious way, honoring my god in this way?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the vines from these constructs are useful for crafting magical items and are valuable.
source_quote: the vines from these constructs are useful for crafting magical items and are valuable.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considers the Shambling Mound’s concealment a security lapse unacceptable in Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Engaging the immediate target while allowing an invisible, grappling threat to remain poised to strike is a lapse in security that any house in Menzoberranzan would never permit.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz finds it peculiar that the Great Seeder is referred to with consistent feminine gender, as myconids have no gender.
source_quote: Daz turns to me, “How odd. Myconids have no gender, and in general get confused about the topic. The sovereign’s use of a specific gender and consistent use of one particular gender is quite peculiar.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has never seen the eldritch horrors that exist here in the realms.
source_quote: I roll my eyes. He has never seen the eldritch horrors that exist here in the realms.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz incinerates the area with a Fireball. The Grik is naturally resistant to fire, but the blast hurts.
source_quote: Daz incinerates the area with a Fireball. The Grik is naturally resistant to fire, but the blast hurts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a knowledgeable observer who recognizes the signs of Zuggtomy’s influence, understands Menzoberranzan’s political metaphors, and uses Shape Water to detect hidden threats.
source_quote: Daz turns to me, “How odd. Myconids have no gender... The sovereign’s use of a specific gender... is quite peculiar.” ... I have seen this before. There is no mystery what this diseased spore is, its power." ... I visualize the terrain as a precise grid, and intend to freeze five-foot cube sections of the moss and water using Shape Water.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a spellcaster who is skeptical of magical oddities, rolls his eyes at Grygum’s reactions, and is methodical in detecting and disarming traps. He uses fairy fire to reveal invisible objects and is attuned to magical residue. He is the one who recognizes the true nature of the Dawnbringer and the false tomb.
source_quote: Daz takes no chances and climbs out of the room into the passageway... I sense some kind of magical trap that was tied to this place.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a tactician who employs Menzoberranzan-style spellcraft and games like K’tharr-li to locate and neutralize threats. He uses Shape Water with grid precision, prioritizing control over brute force.
source_quote: I tell The Ember Vanguard that I have a plan to neutralize the creature’s ability to hide. I explain that I visualize the terrain as a precise grid...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an observer who recognizes the unnatural gendered language used by Phylo as a sign of demonic corruption, draws parallels to drow co-rulership as a sign of weakness and impending death, and understands the nature of the infecting spore without needing to see it.
source_quote: Myconids have no gender, and in general get confused about the topic. The sovereign’s use of a specific gender and consistent use of one particular gender is quite peculiar.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is using Drow-famous tactics, casting Shape Water to freeze water and moss in a checkerboard pattern, playing K’tharr-li to locate the monster, and later incinerating the area with Fireball after the Grick is stunned. He is engaged in technical architectural discussions with Gasbide, revealing deep curiosity about surface-world construction.
source_quote: I'll nerd out with them for a little while.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is using the kinds of tactics the Drow are famous for. He is casting Shape Water, trying to freeze sections of the water and moss in a checkerboard pattern, playing a game he calls K’tharr-li to locate the monster.
source_quote: Daz is using the kinds of tactics the Drow are famous for. He is casting Shape Water, trying to freeze sections of the water and moss in a checkerboard pattern, playing a game he calls K’tharr-li to locate the monster.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz proceeds, launching Scorching Ray attacks. He hits, but the creature is a swamp creature, and the fire is squelched. But still, I can see it is hurt.
source_quote: Daz proceeds, launching Scorching Ray attacks. He hits, but the creature is a swamp creature, and the fire is squelched. But still, I can see it is hurt.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recalls the Menzoberranzan term ‘two in a box’ as a metaphor for co-rulership that leads to death.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, there were tales of two rulers who shared power. We used the term, ‘two in a box’ to describe this power sharing. It wasn’t power sharing; it demonstrated a lack of will on the part of someone... The box from our saying was a metaphor for a tomb.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, despite the halved damage output, reinforces his attack with another Fireball.
source_quote: Daz, despite the halved damage output, reinforces his attack with another Fireball.

subject: Daz
fact: I cannot use Guiding Bolt because Zalthir's spell hides the creature. So, I resort to my secondary option: Tasha's Caustic Brew. It’s essentially projectile acid, hardly glamorous work for a cleric of Bahamut, but necessary to fulfill the mission.
source_quote: I cannot use Guiding Bolt because Zalthir's spell hides the creature. So, I resort to my secondary option: Tasha's Caustic Brew. It’s essentially projectile acid, hardly glamorous work for a cleric of Bahamut, but necessary to fulfill the mission.

subject: Daz
fact: I cast the spell, attempting to burn the creature, but alas, it dodges.
source_quote: I cast the spell, attempting to burn the creature, but alas, it dodges.

subject: Daz
fact: I sense Grygum is worried. I don't know what.
source_quote: I sense Grygum is worried. I don't know what.

subject: Daz
fact: I wonder if this has anything to do with the celebration promised by Phylo tomorrow.
source_quote: I wonder if this has anything to do with the celebration promised by Phylo tomorrow.

subject: Daz
fact: Looking at Zalthir, I pretend to brush my teeth.
source_quote: Looking at Zalthir, I pretend to brush my teeth.

subject: Daz
fact: So Daz continues his game of K’tharr-li and finds the creature.
source_quote: So Daz continues his game of K’tharr-li and finds the creature.

subject: Daz
fact: We arrive at the Northern Terraces of the Neverlight Grove. The terraces lining the northern walls are suffused with faerzress, and I notice that this place is filled with vegetation. As I draw closer, I see water trickling from the walls of this vast cavern being channeled into a crude yet effective terraced irrigation system. A thick, sweet smell fills the air from the thousands of fungi of all colors and sizes, many glowing with a strange, inviting light.

subject: Daz
fact: We return to the Neverlight Grove, the corpse of the Grick dragging slightly.
source_quote: We return to the Neverlight Grove, the corpse of the Grick dragging slightly.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth is a goblin who reports that the party’s pursuers have been lost and are no longer on their trail.
source_quote: Eldeth told us this morning that she believed we had lost them. They were no longer on our trail.

subject: Fargas Rumblefoot
fact: Fargas Rumblefoot warned the party that the tomb they entered was a false one, complete with an easily opened sarcophagus.
source_quote: This was the place that Fargas Rumblefoot warned us of.

subject: Gasbide
fact: "I dream of building a fungal tower even greater than Yggmorgus... I hope to use it to break through the Underdark to the surface world, possibly with the aid of Aromikos," he reveals.
source_quote: "I dream of building a fungal tower even greater than Yggmorgus... I hope to use it to break through the Underdark to the surface world, possibly with the aid of Aromikos," he reveals.

subject: Gasbide
fact: "I dream. Do you want me to tell you what I dream of?".
source_quote: "I dream. Do you want me to tell you what I dream of?".

subject: Gasbide
fact: "You are new to this area!" he exclaims.
source_quote: "You are new to this area!" he exclaims.

subject: Gasbide
